newsitem.title: USA: Clinton looking forward to longest vacation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton looking forward to longest vacation.

text.p: Armed with golf clubs and a stack of books, President Bill Clinton settled in on Monday for the longest vacation he and his family have had in a decade.

Clinton, his wife Hillary and their 17-year-old daughter, Chelsea, arrived late on Sunday for a three-week vacation on Martha's Vineyard, a resort island 7 miles (11 km) off the southeast coast of Massachusetts.

It was their third holiday here since Clinton became president and they were staying on the 20-acre (8 hectares) estate of wealthy Boston developer Richard Friedman in the Oyster Pond area of the island.

It was also a last chance for the U.S. first family to spend a lot of uninterrupted time together before Chelsea goes off to college. She enters California's Stanford University to pursue pre-medical studies in mid-September.

Clinton, newly healed from a serious knee injury suffered in March, is itching to play as much golf as he can. But on his Air Force One plane ride to the Vineyard, he showed a reporter a duffel bag filled with books he plans to read.

He said he was currently reading a biography of John Marshall, who was Supreme Court chief justice in the early 1800s when Thomas Jefferson was president. He said he found the book fascinating because the ideas of Marshall and Jefferson had been so important in shaping the government of the United States.

He also brought along Stephen Ambrose's book about the Lewis and Clark exploration of the American West during Jefferson's presidency, "Undaunted Courage." He said he had read 100 pages of the highly acclaimed book and was looking forward to completing it.

By all accounts from his aides, Clinton has been in need of this vacation, after having worked hard on a balanced-budget deal with the Republican Congress and facing a heavy autumn agenda that could include a fight with some of his fellow Democrats over new trade legislation.
It was shaping up to be, he said, a soujourn of relaxing that would be "the longest in more than a decade" for him and his wife.

The Clintons flew to Martha's Vineyard after a five-hour visit to nearby Block Island, a picturesque hideaway filled with Victorian-era cottages, shops and hotels 12 miles (19 km) off the coast of Rhode Island.

Crowds of fellow vacationers in swimsuits and beachwear turned out to greet the president and his family, who walked along the main street of Old Harbor on the east side of the island shaking hands with the well-wishers as if they were engaged in a political campaign.
The Clintons then stopped at an ice cream shop which had a sign out front inviting them to try the flavor of the week, "Chubby Hubby."

The newly slimmed-down president, who celebrates his 51st birthday on Tuesday with a svelte new look thanks to diet and exercise while rehabilitating his injured right knee, passed up the special in favor of a peach raspberry trifle ice cream cone.
